name: Sacramento
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Sacramento: California state contracting, pension fund counterparties and privacy-aware research.
hero_lede: Sacramento is California's capital, home to the Legislature, state agencies, regulators and the largest public pension funds in the United States. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for matters touching the city and coordinates California-licensed investigators and counsel where local work is required.
intro: Sacramento is the capital of California and the centre of Sacramento County, which had about 1.6 million residents in 2025 according to the county, and of a wider Greater Sacramento region of roughly 2.7 million. Government defines its economy. Public administration employed about 128,000 people in the county in 2025, second only to health care and social assistance with about 145,000. The county also promotes agriculture and food, clean energy technology, information technology and life sciences. Sacramento International Airport handled nearly 13.9 million passengers in 2025. The county's GDP was about 135.5 billion dollars in 2024, and California's state agencies, boards and statewide trade associations are based in or around the city.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Sacramento because the decisions of the world's fourth- or fifth-largest sub-national economy are made there. Companies bidding for state contracts, grants and licences need to know who they are competing with and whether intermediaries are what they claim. Asset managers and counterparties of California's state pension funds face integrity and conflict questions. Regulators headquartered in the region shape privacy, energy, cannabis, insurance and professional licensing across the state, so their enforcement records matter in diligence. And California's privacy, recording and investigator licensing rules, among the strictest in the United States, determine how any fact-finding in the state may lawfully be done.

matters.title: State procurement and grant integrity
matters.text: California agencies award large contracts and grants from Sacramento, including in infrastructure, health, technology and climate programmes. We review published awards, bid protests, lobbying and campaign finance records and corporate links between bidders, subcontractors and officials to support integrity reviews, protests and internal inquiries.

matters.title: Public pension counterparty diligence
matters.text: Asset managers, placement agents and service providers to Sacramento-based public pension funds face scrutiny over conflicts and influence. We research principals' histories, regulatory and litigation records, political contributions and relationships with intermediaries, so clients can address concerns before a mandate is awarded or questioned.

matters.title: Regulatory enforcement history research
matters.text: Many California regulators sit in the Sacramento area. Before acquisitions or partnerships we compile a target's licensing, disciplinary and enforcement record across state boards and agencies, including privacy, insurance, energy and cannabis regulators, and compare it with what the target has disclosed.

matters.title: Lobbying and influence mapping
matters.text: Companies affected by legislation or regulation often need to understand who is lobbying on an issue and on whose behalf. We use Secretary of State lobbying and campaign finance disclosures, coalition filings and media to map relationships, without contacting officials or misrepresenting who we act for.

matters.title: Litigation support in Sacramento courts
matters.text: Suits against state agencies and officials are often filed in Sacramento, and federal cases are heard in the Eastern District of California. We support counsel with party and witness backgrounds, corporate history and document trail reconstruction, scoped to the forum's rules and to California privacy limits.

local_context.title: Courts sitting in Sacramento
local_context.text: The Sacramento County Superior Court hears civil, commercial and criminal cases in the county, and because Sacramento is the capital it receives many actions involving state agencies, including petitions challenging agency decisions. Appeals go to the Third District Court of Appeal, which sits in Sacramento. The US District Court for the Eastern District of California has a Sacramento courthouse for federal fraud, securities and commercial cases. Counsel chooses the forum; we tailor research to it.

local_context.title: California investigator licensing
local_context.text: California licenses private investigators under the Private Investigator Act in Chapter 11.3 of the Business and Professions Code, administered by the Bureau of Security and Investigative Services, based in West Sacramento. Individual licensees need three years of compensated investigative experience or qualifying education plus experience, criminal history checks through the state Department of Justice and FBI, and a written examination. Firms hold a private investigation agency licence. TDSC does not hold a California licence and coordinates California-licensed investigators for any local work.

local_context.title: California privacy and recording rules
local_context.text: California's privacy framework is stricter than most US states. The California Consumer Privacy Act, as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act, gives residents rights over personal information held by covered businesses and is enforced by the Attorney General and the California Privacy Protection Agency, headquartered in Sacramento. The Penal Code generally requires the consent of all parties to record confidential communications and restricts electronic tracking devices. Investigative work is planned with counsel around these limits.

local_context.title: State registries and disclosures
local_context.text: The California Secretary of State in Sacramento maintains business entity records, including statements of information listing officers, directors and agents, as well as lobbying and campaign finance disclosures. State licensing boards publish licence status and disciplinary actions. Real property records for Sacramento are kept by the Sacramento County Clerk-Recorder, with assessment data from the County Assessor, and neighbouring counties hold their own records.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Sacramento and works on Sacramento matters from Nashville. We first agree with the client's counsel what the work must answer, whether a state procurement or grant question, a pension fund relationship, a regulatory history review, an influence map or support for litigation in state or federal court, and how California privacy law bears on it. Research draws on Secretary of State entity, lobbying and campaign finance records, state licensing board and agency enforcement records, county court and property records, federal dockets in the Eastern District of California and media. Any fieldwork, including interviews or observation, is carried out by investigators licensed by the Bureau of Security and Investigative Services, within California recording and tracking restrictions.

faqs.q: Does an investigator need a California licence to work in Sacramento?
faqs.a: Generally yes. The Private Investigator Act requires individuals and firms performing private investigation in California to be licensed by the Bureau of Security and Investigative Services, based in West Sacramento. Requirements include qualifying experience, background checks and an examination. TDSC does not hold a California licence and coordinates licensed California professionals for any local work.

faqs.q: How does California privacy law affect an investigation?
faqs.a: California restricts how personal information is collected and used. The CCPA as amended by the CPRA gives residents rights over their data, the Penal Code generally requires all-party consent to record confidential communications, and electronic tracking devices are restricted. We plan research with counsel so that sources and methods are lawful and that the client's own privacy obligations are respected.

faqs.q: Can you research a California state contract award?
faqs.a: Yes. We review published solicitations, awards and protests, Secretary of State entity records, lobbying and campaign finance disclosures and media to show relationships among bidders, subcontractors, intermediaries and decision-makers. We do not access restricted government systems or contact officials. The work supports counsel in protests, compliance reviews and internal investigations.

faqs.q: Why do pension fund relationships draw scrutiny in Sacramento?
faqs.a: Sacramento hosts some of the largest US public pension funds, and their allocations to external managers are closely watched for conflicts, placement agent fees and political influence. Managers and service providers use background research to confirm that principals, intermediaries and affiliates have no undisclosed relationships or regulatory problems that could later be raised.

faqs.q: Which courts hear disputes involving the State of California?
faqs.a: Many suits against state agencies and officials are filed in the Sacramento County Superior Court, with appeals to the Third District Court of Appeal in Sacramento. Federal claims may go to the Eastern District of California. Forum and procedure are matters for counsel; we provide factual research suited to the court involved.
